newsitem.title: USA: Airline workers swarm Capitol to protest ticket tax.
newsitem.headline: Airline workers swarm Capitol to protest ticket tax.

text.p: About 200 airline workers flown at their companies' expense landed on Capitol Hill Wednesday in a bid to block proposed ticket tax increases.

The Senate version of the bill could add $3.9 billion to airline ticket taxes over five years, although congressional sources said that amount was likely to be reduced as the bill moved through the legislative process.
A spokeswoman representing seven airlines said more than 1,000 workers participated in the rally, although witnesses estimated there were 200 at most.

Uniformed pilots, flight attendants and other workers partially blocked the entrance to the Rayburn Office Building next to the Capitol and caused a traffic jam on nearby Independence Avenue, but a Capitol police spokesman said the rally was orderly and without incident.

"They're concerned about their jobs," airline spokeswoman Linda Harrington Baker said. "We're in the midst of a recovery from the turmoil of years past and they're afraid of how this will affect them."
Most of the employees took on the lobbying mission on their own time and were flown in and out of Washington Wednesday, she said.
One proposal before the House Ways and Means Committee would raise round-trip fees on some international routes from $6 to $31.

The protesters also complained that the Senate version of the bill would single out the U.S. airline industry, favouring foreign carriers by imposing new taxes on the domestic portion of flights to and from overseas.

House Ways and Means Chairman Representative Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, has proposed changes that would reduce the $31 international fee to $20 and address other concerns of the airline industry, a spokesman for Archer said.
